To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) modeling contextual interactions between different objects in an image helps to reduce the uncertainty of the entire image and (b) posing questions which help to learn about contextual concepts is an effective way of obtaining training examples which can be used to learn better classifiers.
we introduce a novel active learning methodology for scene understanding, which utilizes contextual interactions between regions to pose questions and also actively learns contextual concepts.

(1) we introduce a new framework to simultaneously learn both appearance and contextual models, and (2) we introduce new methods to pose labeling questions, and (3) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on two challenging datasets, Pascal VOC 2007 and Caltech 256.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two aspects of active learning: 1) Modeling contextual interactions between regions in the image to pose questions about regions with high uncertainty, which leads to a more effective active learning approach, and 2) Modeling the active learning process as a question answering process, to actively learn about contextual concepts.
developing a framework which utilizes the contextual interactions to actively select the most informative regions for labeling and also to actively learn the contextual concepts.

the following questions: How to select the most informative regions in an image? How to pose the most informative labeling questions? How to utilize the answers to the questions to obtain more relevant training data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach is the first to model the contextual interactions in the image to select the most relevant regions for active learning, which in turn leads to better appearance models and improved performance on multi class classification tasks.

we present an active learning methodology to learn appearance and contextual concepts simultaneously for multi class classification tasks and we introduce a new way of posing labeling questions which helps in actively learning the contextual relationships between concepts and in reducing the overall image entropy.

we propose a novel active learning framework which simultaneously learns appearance and contextual models, by utilizing the contextual interactions and relationships between different regions in an image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel framework for active learning for multi class classification tasks.
it is a novel approach to active learning for scene understanding tasks, which simultaneously learns appearance and contextual models.
our approach learns contextual models for scene classification and utilizes the contextual knowledge in active learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active learning problem is not about selecting the most ambiguous region, but about selecting the most informative region for learning.

by explicitly modeling contextual interactions and posing questions in a manner which mimics the human way of actively learning about the environment, one can significantly reduce the number of labeled training examples required to train an appearance model.
by modeling the contextual interactions between image regions, we can obtain better models and reduce the number of training examples required to learn the models.
